why.text: Limestone soils sit under a Mediterranean climate with a cold, drying wind. The wines are fresh, with medium-high acidity and a mineral touch.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, some barrel-fermented or aged; sweet whites from botrytised grapes; liqueur wines from Moscatel de Grano Menudo.

climate.text: Mediterranean with Atlantic influence in the northwest; a cold, drying wind prevails; 400 to 500 mm of rain on average.

soil.text: High in limestone, moderately stony, with a clay-loam texture.

tastes.text: Reds: purple to cherry; fruity, medium body, ripe tannin; aged ones garnet to ruby with spice. Whites: pale to straw, green reflections; fruity, floral, fresh. Rosés: pale pink to raspberry; fruity, fresh.

styles.name: Uvas botritizadas
styles.text: White from botrytised grapes: pale yellow, fruity, floral, fresh.

styles.name: Fermentado en barrica
styles.text: White, rosé or red fermented in oak; fruit with toasty barrel notes.

styles.name: Crianza
styles.text: Red garnet to cherry; fruit with barrel notes; soft, intense tannins.

styles.name: Reserva
styles.text: Red cherry to ruby; ripe fruit and spice; powerful, round, ripe tannin.

why.text: August and September swing strongly between warm and cool, and the soils are distinctive. The wines are fruity and aromatic, with high acidity.

styles.text: Whites, rosados, sparkling wines and reds; also naturally sweet, late-harvest and liqueur wines.

climate.text: Strong temperature contrast in August and September, which favours the wines' aroma.

soil.text: No soil type is named; the document says the soils give fruity, alcoholic, high-acid wines.

tastes.text: Whites: straw to gold; fruity or floral. Rosés: violet-pink to strawberry; fruity. Reds: violet-red to cherry; fresh, fruity, some milky notes.

styles.name: Vendimia tardía
styles.text: Whites golden with fruit, toast, vanilla; reds with candied fruit, raisins.

styles.name: Naturalmente dulce
styles.text: Whites straw to gold with candied or dried fruit; reds fresh and sweet.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Whites straw to gold, reds cherry-red; candied fruit, full-bodied, sweet.

why.text: Scant rain and the dry cierzo wind keep vines under constant water stress. Ripening is slow, so the wines gain aroma and deep colour.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also sparkling, naturally sweet, late-harvest and liqueur wines.

climate.text: Little rain, the cierzo wind and abrupt temperature changes; the wind dries the soil and limits humidity.

tastes.text: Reds: clear cherry; ripe, floral fruit; long, smooth, structured, fleshy. Whites and rosés: floral, fruity; fresh, acidic.

styles.name: Vendimia tardía, Naturalmente dulce, Vino de licor
styles.text: Intense, clean aromas; candied or dried fruit; pleasantly sweet.

why.text: Vines grow on flat ground at about 460 to 495 m, in deep, stony soils. A dry climate and the cierzo wind suit them.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and dry reds, including carbonic-maceration and barrel-aged reds.

climate.text: Dry: about 423 mm of rain a year, dry summers, frost mid-October to April; the cierzo wind guards against fungal disease.

soil.text: Loam soils (sandy, sandy-clay and clay loams), deep, well drained and low in humus.

altitude.text: 460 to 495 m above sea level; the relief is nearly flat.

tastes.text: Reds: ripe cherry, violet to ruby; floral, red and black fruit; soft, complex. Whites: pale green-straw; floral, orchard, stone and tropical fruit; lively. Rosés: pink with violet; floral, red fruit.

styles.name: Maceración carbónica
styles.text: Red, cherry with purple tones; floral, balsamic, red and black fruit; long.

styles.name: Barrica
styles.text: Red; ripe red and black fruit, nuts, balsamic; fruit leads over oak.

styles.name: Vendimia seleccionada
styles.text: Red, ripe cherry with garnet; ripe fruit, toast, dried fruit; ripe tannins.

why.text: Little rain and extreme temperatures, with the cierzo wind, make a harsh setting. Only hardy vineyards have kept going.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also sparkling, needle, sweet, late-harvest and liqueur wines.

climate.text: Low rainfall, extreme temperatures and the cierzo wind.

tastes.text: Reds: deep purple-cherry with violet to ruby glints; intense ripe red fruit; fleshy, dry. Whites: pale yellow; fresh, fruity, soft, light. Rosés: pink with violet to salmon; fresh, fruity.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: White, rosé or red; fresh and light, with a light prickle.

styles.name: Vendimia tardía
styles.text: Ripe-fruit aromas; glycerine, not acidic; structured with sweet tannins.

styles.name: Naturalmente dulce
styles.text: White or red; floral, honeyed; intense, sweet, long.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: White or red; floral, honeyed; intense, structured, sweet, fruity.

why.text: Altitude and big day-night swings slow ripening. The wines are structured, with colour and a mineral edge.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also naturally sweet, late-harvest, needle, sparkling and liqueur wines.

climate.text: Large temperature differences between day and night while the grapes ripen; vines at altitude get strong sun.

soil.text: A wide range of soils; the document names no single main type.

tastes.text: Reds: cherry to dark garnet; intense fruit and flowers; tasty, fleshy, soft tannin. Whites: pale straw, fresh fruit; fresh, slightly acid. Rosés: strawberry to raspberry; floral, red fruit.

styles.name: Calatayud Superior
styles.text: Red of deep cherry to ruby colour; fruit, balsamic, toast and spice.

styles.name: Vendimia tardía
styles.text: Golden whites to dark purple reds; floral, fresh, silky, persistent.

styles.name: Naturalmente dulce
styles.text: White or red; ripe and candied fruit, silky, rich, sweet.
